aiControl.title: AI Center
aiControl.sub: Every AI agent: what it is doing, what it cost, what it decided.

master.label: MASTER SWITCH
master.onBody: {n} agent(s) are working inside their caps and limits.
master.offBody: Off until it is turned on. With AI off nothing is sent to any AI company, and every AI feature falls back to its rule or saved template — the shop keeps running as normal.
master.switchLabel: AI master switch: on or off
master.capWarn: No monthly spend cap is set yet. Set one in AI costs so spending can never run away.
master.toastOff: AI is off — the shop keeps running on rules and templates
master.toastFailed: Could not change the AI master switch

agents.title: Agents
agents.sub: Each agent's own switch; the master switch above decides whether any of them may actually work — unless an agent is kept on.
agents.statusWorkingKeptOn: Working — kept on while AI is off
agents.readOnly: You can see the agents; pausing or resuming one needs the AI control permission.

keepOn.label: Keep on even when AI is off
keepOn.switchLabel: Keep {name} on even when AI is off
keepOn.pillOn: Kept on even when AI is off
keepOn.toastOn: {name} will keep working even when AI is off
keepOn.toastOff: {name} now pauses with the master switch

model.label: Model
model.noteSame: This is Claude's own recommended pick for this agent today.
model.noteChanged: This works too. Per-run cost and quality comparisons will show once the AI Cost Book is built (PR 312).
model.noteFallback: {provider} is no longer Tested, so {name} is quietly using the practice writer until it is Tested again or you pick again.
model.noteRouted: {name} handles personal or business data, so a free-capable connection is never used for it — it is actually using {effective} instead.
model.toastNotReady: Test that connection in Keys & connections first

schedule.label: Schedule
schedule.always: No time restriction — it only acts on its own triggers, any time.
schedule.nextRunNone: Nothing time-based to preview — it only acts on its own triggers.
schedule.toastInvalid: Pick a clock time (and, for Weekly, at least one day) first

cap.label: Monthly spend cap
cap.toastInvalid: Enter a whole amount above zero, or leave it empty for no cap

routing.title: Which data may reach which model
routing.sub: Locked policy (Blueprint A5.2): personal and business data only ever reach a paid connection; only reviewed public/draft work may use a free-capable one. The owner cannot change this from here.
routing.note: If an agent's own model pick would break this rule, the page quietly uses a paid connection instead and says so under that agent's model.

personal.name: Personal
personal.rule: A customer's name, phone, address, chat or order. Paid connections only — never a free one.

business.name: Business
business.rule: The shop's own sales, cost, stock or report figures. Paid connections only — a free one is not recommended.

publicDraft.name: Public / draft
publicDraft.rule: Content a person reviews before it goes out (blog, SEO, social copy). A free-capable connection is allowed, with an automatic paid fallback.

aiCostBook.title: AI Cost Book
aiCostBook.sub: What every AI job in the shop costs, and which model it uses — before any money is spent.
aiCostBook.noRate: No USD rate is typed yet, so costs are shown in USD. To see them in ৳, set a USD rate in Money › Costs & fees.
aiCostBook.honestNote: Text jobs are cheap. Image generation is far more expensive, and video assembly costs server time rather than tokens. Voice transcription is cheap too. These estimates carry a ±10–15% band for now. Once a job has 5 real runs, its own Actual column shows what it really cost, so the estimate is checked against reality instead of staying a guess.

search.label: Search the Cost Book
search.placeholder: Search — e.g. blog, support, reel, photoshoot

aiCostBook.actualNone: No real data yet — shown once {min} real runs exist.

presets.title: One-click presets
presets.changed: {n} jobs would change model ({smaller} to a smaller model, {larger} to a larger one)
presets.noChange: Already the current pick for every job.

calc.title: Calculator — describe a piece of work
calc.scaleHint: Bigger or smaller than the job's usual run, e.g. a longer article. Leave blank for 1×.
calc.savePlaceholder: e.g. "10 blog posts with images, November"
calc.invalid: Fill in a job and a whole number of runs for every line
calc.needPermission: "AI control" is needed to use the calculator.

aiApprovals.title: Approvals
aiApprovals.sub: Everything an AI agent wants to do but may not do alone, in one queue — clear it in one pass.

pending.label: Waiting
pending.empty: Nothing is waiting — no agent can act on its own yet.
pending.toastAlready: Someone already decided this one — the list below has been refreshed
pending.needPermission: You don't have permission to decide this one. You can still see the queue.

decided.label: Decision history
decided.sub: The most recent {n} decided, expired or cancelled requests — the rest stay in the database, just not shown here.

aiPermissions.title: Permission matrix
aiPermissions.sub: What each agent may decide alone, must only propose, or may not touch at all.
aiPermissions.intro: No agent can decide anything alone until you widen a cell below from "Must ask first" — that is the safe starting point for every agent and every resource.

levelHint.alone: Acts on its own, no approval needed.
levelHint.propose: May only ask — lands in Approvals for your decision.
levelHint.none: May not touch this at all, not even to ask.

aiPermissions.readOnly: You can see the matrix but not change it.
aiPermissions.needPermission: "AI control" is needed to change this matrix.

aiDiary.title: AI diary
aiDiary.sub: What each agent did, why, and what it changed — in plain Bengali, never a technical log.
aiDiary.empty: Nothing yet — no agent has written to the diary.

aiSkills.title: Skills
aiSkills.sub: What the agents know how to do. A new or imported skill needs the owner's approval before it runs.
aiSkills.needPermission: You can see the skill library, but importing, rolling back or switching a skill needs permission.
aiSkills.empty: No skills yet — import one, or wait for an agent's own proposal from Site health.

dialog.title: Import a skill
dialog.namePlaceholder: e.g. Eid size reminder message draft
dialog.effect1: The skill is added, waiting for approval
dialog.effect2: It goes to Approvals — it only runs once a person approves it

rollback.effect: v{from} stays in history; v{to} becomes the current version
rollback.toastFailed: Could not roll this skill back
